claims.text: Paragraph 6 carries the deniability test in substantially the words NSC 10/2 used six years earlier: covert operations are to be so planned and executed that 'any U.S. Government responsibility for them is not evident to unauthorized persons and that if uncovered the U.S. Government can plausibly disclaim any responsibility.'

claims.text: NSC 5412 DOES NOT CREATE THE 5412 COMMITTEE, and the widely repeated claim that it does is not supported by the document. No Special Group and no committee of that name appears anywhere in the text. The State Department's own editorial note attributes the Special Group to NSC 5412/2 of 28 December 1955, and says the body became known as the 'NSC 5412/2 Special Group'.

timeline.label: NSC 5412 replaces the 1948 covert-action charter
timeline.text: The President approves NSC 5412 the day it is circulated. It supersedes NSC 10/2 and NSC 10/5, keeps the authority in section 102(d)(5), restates the plausible-deniability test almost word for word, and makes the Operations Coordinating Board the normal channel for interagency support. It does not create the Special Group; that comes with NSC 5412/2 in December 1955.
